claim: AAAI-26 received almost 29,000 Main Track submissions, of which roughly 23,000 survived compliance checks and entered review, nearly double AAAI-25's volume.
stance_target: scale of the AAAI acceptance bar / competitive pressure
quoted_support: AAAI-26 received almost 29,000 submissions to the Main Technical Track... we still have roughly 23,000 papers under review -- nearly twice the number of papers reviewed by AAAI-25!

claim: The three largest keyword areas for AAAI-26 submissions were Computer Vision (~10,000), Machine Learning (~8,000), and Natural Language Processing (4,000+), meaning calibration/code-LLM work competes inside the most saturated subareas.
stance_target: competitive density of DPRC's subarea at AAAI
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track submission keyword distribution
quoted_support: The three largest research primary keywords for AAAI-26 submissions are Computer Vision (nearly 10,000), Machine Learning (nearly 8,000), and Natural Language Processing (over 4,000).

claim: At AAAI-26's submission scale, some reviewers are assigned papers adjacent to rather than squarely within their core expertise, meaning borderline papers may face reviewers who need the paper to be self-contained rather than assuming deep subfield context.
stance_target: borderline papers benefit from unambiguous, self-contained framing at AAAI
quoted_support: Given the extreme volume of submissions and the fact that we do not have an equal number of reviewers and papers in each subarea, some reviewers are assessing papers that are adjacent to (rather than squarely within) their core area of expertise.
